eliyah_rabbah.he: [א] זמן קריאת שמע וכו'. ומברכין שתים לפניה ואחת לאחריה ובערב שתים לפניה ושתים לאחריה וסמכום על פסוק שבע ביום הללתיך (טור) וכתב הלבוש לפי שקדם ערב לבוקר דכתיב ויהי ערב ויהי בוקר לקחו ארבע שהם הרוב לערבית, עד כאן. פירוש דקשיא ליה למה תיקנו בערבית ברכה אחת יותר משחרית. אבל ראיתי בשוחר טוב סימן ו' שבע ביום הללתיך, אמר ר' יהושע בן לוי אלו שבע מצוות שבקריאת שמע יוצר אור, ואהבה, שמע, והיה אם שמוע, ויאמר, אמת ויציב, גאל ישראל ולפי שאין מצות ציצית בלילה מוסיף ברכה, עד כאן. גם צריך עיון דמלבוש משמע דפירש פסוק דשבע ביום הללתיך על שבע ברכות דשחרית וערבית יחד, וכן פירש בית יוסף לקמן ריש סימן רל"ו דברי הטור שהביא ירושלמי, ר' יהושע בן לוי אמר על שם שבע ביום הללתיך, וכן משמע בפירוש רש"י דף י"א ותוס' ריש ברכות, וצריך עיון דכיון דבירושלמי נמי דברי ר' יהושע בן לוי הן מסתמא פירשו על שבע מצוות ולכן התקינו ברכות אלו שיהיה שבע ביום ושבע בלילה, וכדברי מדרש שוחר טוב. מיהו בזה יש לומר דסבירא ליה דתרתי שמעית מקרא זה שבע מצוות גם שבע ברכות. ומכל מקום הא יש לנו טעם מרווח על שתיקנו ארבע בערבית, אך אפשר דסבירא ליה ללבוש דזה לבני מערבא שלא היו אומרים פרשת ויאמר בערבית כדאיתא בברכות דף י"ד, אבל לדידן דאמרינן ויאמר לא היה לנו להוסיף ברכה לכן הוצרך הלבוש לטעם אחר. ומכל מקום יש לומר כיון שאין מצות ציצית נוהגת בלילה לא חשבינן לאמירה למצוה, וכן ברוקח סימן שי"ט כתב טעם זה בשם רבינו תם. ועוד כתב טעם באבודרהם בשם הראב"ד ז"ל נתנו היתירה לערבית מפני שתפילת ערבית רשות ובעינן שיהיו שוין:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [1] "The time of Kriat Shema," etc. And one blesses two before it and one after it; and in the evening two before it and two after it; and they based them on the verse "seven times a day I praise You" (Tur); and Levush wrote: because evening preceded morning in the order of time, as it is written "and there was evening and there was morning," therefore they took the four—which are the majority—for the evening [service], until here. The explanation: he was troubled why they instituted one more blessing in the evening than in the morning. But I have seen in Shocher Tov siman 6: "Seven times a day I praise You"—R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: these are the seven commandments in Kriat Shema: Yotzer Or, Ahavah, Shema, Ve-hayah im shamoa, Va-yomer, Emet veYatziv, Ga'al Yisrael; and because the mitzvah of tzitzit does not apply at night, they add a blessing—until here. It also requires examination: from Levush it appears he interpreted the verse "seven times a day I praise You" on the seven blessings of morning and evening together; and likewise Beit Yosef explained later at the beginning of siman 236 the words of Tur who brought Yerushalmi: R. Yehoshua ben Levi said on the name "seven times a day I praise You"; and likewise it appears from Rashi's explanation folio 11 and Tosafot at the beginning of Berakhot; and it requires examination: since in Yerushalmi too the words of R. Yehoshua ben Levi are [cited], presumably they interpreted on the seven commandments; and therefore they instituted these blessings so there would be seven by day and seven by night, as the midrash Shocher Tov [says]. However, one may say that he holds there are two readings of this verse: seven commandments and also seven blessings. And in any case we have a broad reason why they instituted four in the evening; but it is possible he holds like Levush that this is for the people of the West who would not say the section Va-yomer in the evening, as is stated in Berakhot folio 14; but for us who say Va-yomer we should not have added a blessing; therefore Levush needed another reason. And in any case one may say: since the mitzvah of tzitzit does not apply at night, we do not count its recitation as a mitzvah; and likewise Rokeach siman 319 wrote this reason in the name of Rabbeinu Tam. And he also wrote a reason in Avudraham in the name of Raavad—may his memory be blessed: they gave the extra [blessing] to the evening because the evening prayer is optional and we want them to be equal.

kaf_hachayim.en: (1) [Seif 1] The time of the morning Kriat Shema, etc. And one blesses two before it and one after it; and in the evening two before it and two after it; and they based them on the verse "seven times a day I praise You," etc.—Tur; and see in Sefer haTikkunim end of tikkun 12 the reason for these seven blessings; and the reason they arranged four blessings in the evening and three in the morning—Levush wrote: because in the order of time evening preceded morning, as it is written "and there was evening and there was morning," etc., therefore they took the four—which are the majority—for the evening, which comes first, and left the remaining three for the morning—so his words; and R. Avudraham folio 1b wrote the reason in the name of Raavad: they gave the extra to the evening because the evening prayer is optional and we want them to be equal. In the Gemara page 3a in Tosafot, etc.—for it was taught: R' Eliezer says three watches there are in the night. And a sign for the matter: at the beginning of watch one a donkey brays, etc.; watch two, etc.; watch three, etc. And it challenges: what does he count? If the beginning of a watch is considered—for watch one why do I need a sign? It is evening—meaning the beginning of the night is evident. And it answers: in truth the end of a watch is considered, and it was necessary to give a sign for the end of watch three for one who sleeps in a dark house and does not know the time of Keriat Shema—when he sees the sign of the end of watch three he rises and reads. And Tosafot challenged well; rather Magen Avraham's intention is that I do not know the time of the end of watch three whether it is alot hashachar or hanetz hachama; therefore Magen Avraham hinted to look in the Gemara and Tosafot—for from those words of Tosafot it is proven that the end of watch three is alot hashachar, for they wrote in their answer: once he knows when alot hashachar will be before he rises, etc.—therefore the end of watch three is alot hashachar. Rather four watches there are in the night. And from midnight until the end of the night are two watches and the verses do not contradict each other. And R' Natan holds three watches in the night. And the Gemara challenges: if so, for R' Natan the verses are difficult—for from midnight onward there is only a watch and a half; and how did he say "my eyes precede the watches" implying two? And it answers: R' Natan holds like R' Yehuda who said the time of Keriat Shema is until three hours, for thus is the way of the sons of kings to stand at three hours; therefore he said that alot hashachar "my eyes precede the watches" compared to other kings—for since he rose at midnight there are six of the night and two of the day, and Rashi explains two of the day—that other kings sleep (and the third hour should be as Magen Avraham wrote seif katan 6 there)—behold two watches, that is eight hours together. And for R' Natan, since the night is twelve hours and there are only three watches, each watch reaches four hours—if so two watches are eight hours. And the verse "my eyes precede the watches" fits this, end of the Gemara. And since Magen Avraham already proved from the words of Tosafot that the end of the watches are alot hashachar—if so it is impossible that the three hours of the sons of kings are from hanetz hachama—for then there is more than two hours of day—for there is continuation of time from alot hashachar until hanetz hachama (and according to Bach seif katan 2 it is an hour)—if so it must be that the three hours are certainly counted from alot hashachar.
